name: Cod à la Nage (Poached in Broth) With Coconut Milk, Lime, and Lemongrass

ingredients.name: fresh Thai red chile, stemmed and thinly sliced
lime juice, plus extra wedges for serving

instructions.primary_message: In a large, straight-sided sauté pan, heat oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add shallot, garlic, and chile and cook, stirring, until vegetables are softened and shallot is translucent, about 2 minutes.

Add coconut milk (and broth, if using; see notes), fish sauce, lime peel, ginger, lemongrass, cilantro sprigs, and basil sprigs. Season cod with salt and pepper, then nestle in coconut broth; the fish should be partially submerged. Bring liquid to a simmer, then cover pan and lower heat. Cook, covered, until cod is just cooked through and registers 57°C on an instant-read thermometer, about 5 minutes.

Using a slotted spatula, transfer cod to bowls. Whisk lime juice into broth. Season broth with salt and pepper, then ladle all around fish in the bowls along with the vegetables. Garnish with cilantro and basil leaves. Serve right away with lime wedges on the side.

description: Gently poach cod in a broth of coconut milk, lemongrass, ginger, fresh chiles, and fish sauce for an easy and flavorful dinner.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 2 sprigs fresh cilantro, plus picked leaves for garnish; 2 sprigs basil, preferably Thai basil, plus torn leaves for garnish

Optional substitutions: fresh Thai red chile → Fresno pepper

Notes: Using all coconut milk makes a thicker, richer broth; for a lighter version, use only one can of coconut milk and replace the other with 397 g of vegetable or fish broth.
author: Daniel Gritzer
